name: Datum Layout
tagline: 3D plant layout and piping: place equipment, route lines, check and hand over.
for: Piping and layout designers, mechanical and process engineers, and students learning plant design.
about: Datum Layout lays out one plant in 3D. You place equipment from its datasheet sizes, route pipes between nozzles, and the elbows, tees, flanges and valves appear and size themselves from the line's size and pipe class. Every part is generated from a dimension table and a shape rule, so nothing is downloaded and every dimension has a source.

Then it checks the model for clashes, open ends, spec problems and differences with the line list, lists every line, the equipment with its nozzles and the material take-off, and hands each line to Datum Pipe as a piping component file for its isometric and stress analysis. Lines can also come in from a piping component file.

steps.title: Place the equipment
steps.text: Drag vessels, drums, tanks, columns, pumps and exchangers onto the plot and set their sizes and nozzles from the datasheet.

steps.title: Route the lines
steps.text: Click from nozzle to nozzle: spec elbows, reducers and flanges appear by themselves. Drag valves and tees onto a pipe and they snap, size themselves and split it.

steps.title: Check and hand over
steps.text: Find clashes, open ends and class problems, export the line list and material take-off, and send each line to Datum Pipe.

highlights: A workspace laid out in the order of the work: a steps bar, a plant tree with filters and eyes to show or hide each item, a context bar and a tool strip
Six parametric equipment types with nozzles: vertical vessel, horizontal drum, storage tank, column, centrifugal pump with motor and baseplate, shell-and-tube exchanger
Routing with orthogonal guides: long- or short-radius elbows at every turn, reducers where sizes change, weld-neck flanges, gaskets and bolt sets at flanged nozzles
Drag corners, add or remove jogs, move runs: the elbows follow and components stay put
Drag and drop valves, strainers, flange pairs, tees and reducers that snap onto the pipe by their ports; a tee starts a branch
Select several items to move, copy, turn, mirror or delete them together
Colour by line, class, fluid or size; hide, isolate, section box, measure and saved views
Clash check (pipe–pipe, pipe–equipment, pipe–ground) with a clearance, plus open ends, mismatches, class rules, line numbers and the line list
Line list, equipment and nozzle list, and material take-off per line, all to CSV; a line list CSV read back to check against
PCF export that Datum Pipe reads unchanged, PCF import, and glTF 2.0 for any 3D viewer
A catalogue of generated parts (½" to 24", flanges class 150 to 2500, valves in every class) with every row's source, eight example pipe classes, and plug-in packs

roadmap.title: Spec-driven piping in 3D
items: Plot, six equipment types, routing with automatic elbows, reducers and flanges
Drag-and-drop fittings that snap and split
Clash and spec checks, lists, PCF for Datum Pipe, glTF

roadmap.title: Working like a layout designer
items: Flanges to class 2500, valves in every class, eight example pipe classes, a measure tool
Select several items; move, copy, turn, mirror and delete them together
Move corners and add or remove jogs; colour by line, class, fluid or size; hide, isolate, section box
Saved views; a line list to check against; lines from piping component files
The workspace: steps bar, plant tree, context bar and tool strip
A valve list, butt welds in the take-off, design-rule checks

roadmap.title: Pipe classes and fittings

Eccentric reducers, crosses, sloped lines
Design rules for supports and access (with 0.3's steel)

Pipe supports (rest, guide, anchor, shoe) placed on lines and sent to Datum Pipe with the PCF

roadmap.title: Drawings and quantities

Place equipment and route its lines from the package
A 3D-against-P&ID check: missing or extra components, wrong order, wrong size, unconnected lines
More pipe classes as plug-in packs

roadmap.title: CAD exchange
